paper.title: Learning to Play Sequential Games versus Unknown Opponents

settings.name_in_paper: Repeated sequential game versus adversarial sequence of unknown opponent types
unmapped: Learner's reward r(x,y) in [0,1] is known and L_r-Lipschitz; the unknown part is the opponent response function b(x,theta) in an RKHS with norm <= B over (action, type) inputs
The opponent type theta_t (chosen by an adaptive adversary) is revealed after the learner acts
Learner observes a noisy opponent response y_t = b(x_t, theta_t) + eps_t rather than its reward directly
settings.definition_quote: In every round $t$: The learner computes a randomized strategy $\p_t$ ... The opponent observes $x_t$ and responds by selecting $ y_t = b(x_t,\theta_t)$ ... The learner observes the opponent's type $\theta_t$ and response $y_t$, and receives reward $r(x_t, y_t)$. The opponent's types can be chosen by an adaptive adversary

settings.name_in_paper: Single opponent type (bilevel optimization with unknown lower-level function)
unmapped: Objective r(x, b(x, theta_bar)) with known L_r-Lipschitz reward r and unknown RKHS response function b; learner observes noisy response y_t, not reward
settings.definition_quote: We now consider the special case where the learner is playing against the opponent of a single \emph{known} type at every round of the game, i.e., $\theta_t = \bar{\theta}$.

settings.name_in_paper: Repeated Stackelberg games with unknown follower utilities
unmapped: Leader's action is a mixed strategy in the n_l-simplex; follower best-responds via unknown utility; best-response function in RKHS and L_b-Lipschitz
Learner knows Lipschitz constants L_r and L_b (used to build the discretization)
Follower type revealed after acting; leader reward known and L_r-Lipschitz; learner observes noisy follower response
settings.definition_quote: we can map repeated Stackelberg games to our setup by letting $x_t \in \mathcal{X} = \Delta^{n_l}$ be the leader's mixed strategy at time $t$ ... the opponent's response function in a Stackelberg game assumes the specific \emph{best-response} form $b(x_t,\theta_t) = \argmax_{y \in \mathcal{Y}} U_{\theta_t}(x_t,y)$

algorithms.name: Bilevel optimistic strategy (argmax of optimistic reward, eq. algorithm_single_opponent)
StackelUCB over discretized mixed-strategy grid D

symbols.beta_T: confidence parameter sigma*lam^{-1}*sqrt(2 log(1/delta) + log det(I_T + K_T/lam)) + lam^{-1/2} B

conditions: reward r: X x Y -> [0,1] is L_r-Lipschitz
finite action set X with |X| = K
tuning: beta_t = sigma lam^{-1} sqrt(2 log(1/delta) + log det(I_t + K_t/lam)) + lam^{-1/2} B

source.label: thm:thm2
source.quote: Then for any $\delta \in (0,1)$, the regret of \ouralg when used with $\lambda \geq 1$, $\beta_t = ...$, and learning step $\eta = \sqrt{8 \log(|\mathcal{X}|)/T}$, is bounded, with probability at least $1-2\delta$, by R(T) \leq \sqrt{\tfrac{1}{2}T \log |\mathcal{X}|}  + \sqrt{ \tfrac{1}{2}T\log{(\tfrac{1}{\delta})}} + \ 4 L_r \beta_T \sqrt{T \lambda \gamma_T}

results.notes: Holds with probability >= 1-2delta. Regret is realized regret against best fixed action in hindsight (with true responses). K = |X|. Compute polynomial assuming the inner max over y of r(x,y) is efficient.

conditions: reward r: X x Y -> [0,1] is L_r-Lipschitz
same opponent type theta_bar every round

source.label: thm:Theorem1
source.quote: Then for any $\delta \in (0,1)$, the regret of the learner when playing according to~\eqref{eq:algorithm_single_opponent} with $\beta_t$ set as in Theorem~\ref{thm:thm2} and $\lambda \geq 1$, is bounded with probability at least $1-\delta$ by R(T) \leq 4 L_r  \beta_T \sqrt{T \lambda \gamma_T}

results.notes: Probability 1-delta. Algorithm does not use T, so anytime.

bound.expression_latex: \sqrt{ \tfrac{1}{2} T  n_l \log \big(L_r (1 + L_b) \sqrt{n_l T}\big)} + \sqrt{T n_l } + \sqrt{\tfrac{1}{2} T \log{\big(\tfrac{1}{\delta}\big)}} + \ 4 L_r \beta_T \sqrt{T \lambda \gamma_T}

symbols.L_b: Lipschitz constant of follower best-response function

tuning: D uniform grid with |D| = (L_r(1+L_b) sqrt(n_l T))^{n_l}
